They use resolved HCO+ maps and compare them with the Hill5 model. Best fits pin the inward speed near the center between six tenths and one point six kilometers per second. Line widths once blamed on turbulence instead reflect ordered infall inside the beam. Oddly, infall slows at mid-radius and speeds up both inward and outward.
arxiv-2604-00029: Zhao and team propose UM-PINN, a system for training physics-informed neural networks as multi-task learning under steady uncertainty. Physics-informed neural networks struggle with shock waves in high-speed flows, a failure attributed to gradient trouble. A space mask with tunable variance values trades equation errors and initial conditions across the domain, steadied by Sobol samples. The team tests the system on the Sod shock tube, Shu-Osher problem, and Riemann case, where schemes fail. UM-PINN improves accuracy and sharpness by orders of magnitude over rivals.
arxiv-2604-00229: Kun Qin and Trinitis study timing in quantum key distribution, where FPGA converter flaws can shift coincidence timing. Such converters show intrinsic nonlinearity, usually dismissed as calibration, yet raw nonuniformity shifts coincidence timing and raises the quantum bit error rate. Their model combines random timing jitter with fixed nonlinearity, and fabric fixes use LUT-aided delay shaping and placement constraints without tuning. Testing two open-source time-to-digital converters on Zynq-7000, they cut integral nonlinearity by 14 to 21 percent and lift the likely secret fraction by about 4 to 14 percent.
arxiv-2604-00329: Kamimura and seven colleagues model cheetah high-speed running with a planar model using asymmetric spinal stiffness, searching periodic bounding solutions across stiffness values. Cheetah-like solutions extend the spine after hindlimb liftoff and flex it after forelimb liftoff; the rest reverse that pattern. Under asymmetric stiffness, cheetah-like solutions cut ground reaction forces while holding horizontal velocity better. Spinal-motion timing against stance timing decides high-speed performance, suggesting design rules for spined legged robots.
arxiv-2604-00829: Irawan and colleagues propose LinguDistill, an adapter-free distillation method. It recovers language ability lost when a pretrained language model is turned into a vision-language model. A frozen original model teaches during multimodal training through layer-wise KV-cache sharing, with distillation applied only on language-heavy data. The method matches the original vision-language model on text-only benchmarks on average, beats it on ScienceQA, and adds no parameters or inference cost.
arxiv-2604-01129: Zhang and colleagues present ReinDriveGen, a framework giving control over scenes, letting users edit trajectories to stage corner cases like collisions, drifting and spinning vehicles, jaywalkers and lane-cutting cyclists. It builds a 3D point cloud scene from LiDAR data, completes vehicle views to 360-degree geometry, and renders it into 2D images guiding a diffusion model. Since scenes fall outside training, RL-based post-training with preference and reward models improves quality without ground-truth supervision. Tests show it beating approaches on edited scenes and topping viewpoint synthesis.
arxiv-2604-01229: Qiu and colleagues propose IBAM, a neural-assisted physics-based framework for interpretable battery aging that needs no extra diagnostic tests. State of health alone is a single number with limited meaning, since two batteries at the same value can degrade very differently. IBAM outputs a two-dimensional aging fingerprint from routine battery management logs, capturing curve-wide polarization voltage loss and tail loss near end of discharge. Across short-, medium-, and long-lived batteries, it gives the most faithful physics models at each aging stage and clarifies degradation mechanisms.
arxiv-2604-01329: Abdel Hameed and colleagues rework model merging, the cheap trick of blending separately trained models so one model inherits each one's skills. Framing merging as layer-by-layer minimization of interference normally demands covariance matrices estimated from data, which may be unavailable. They show that under certain conditions those matrices can be read off the models' difference matrices instead. That removes the data need and cuts cost. Across vision and language tests, on models from 86 million to 7 billion parameters, their data-free method beats prior data-free methods.
arxiv-2604-01829: Haeupler, Long, Roeyskoe and Saranurak give the first distance labeling scheme with constant approximation under edge failures, settling a problem from Dory and Parter. Each vertex and edge gets a label. After faulty edges are removed, the distance between two points can be approximated from those edge labels plus the points. Their polynomial-time scheme reaches constant approximation with compact labels, improving on earlier schemes that managed only growing approximation. It sharpens sensitivity oracles, where logarithmically many faults forced slow queries, linearly growing approximation, or exponentially worse dependence on k.
arxiv-2604-01929: Hadjeres and colleagues present Woosh, Sony AI's open foundation model for sound effects. Audio researchers rely on open generative models as baselines and building blocks. Woosh supplies a high-quality audio encoder-decoder, a text-audio alignment model for conditioning, and text-to-audio plus video-to-audio generators, with distilled versions for low-resource, fast use. Tests on public and private data show each part matching or beating open rivals such as StableAudio-Open and TangoFlux. Code, weights and demo samples are released alongside the report.
arxiv-2604-02329: Huang and colleagues build a large dynamic dataset for generative rendering from AAA games. A dual screen stitched capture yields 4M continuous frames of RGB plus five G-buffer channels across varied scenes, weather and motion blur. The data support both inverse rendering, splitting geometry and materials in the wild, and forward rendering, generating video guided by G-buffers. Inverse renderers tuned on the data generalize better across datasets, and a new vision language model assessment of semantic, spatial and temporal consistency tracks human judgment.
arxiv-2604-02529: Hood and colleagues release the first public set of brightness histories for active galactic nuclei watched by the South Pole Telescope. The release holds 158 light curves from the SPTpol camera, which ran from 2012 to 2016 and scanned a 500-square-degree sky patch several times a day. The team finds a strong link between brightness flicker and spectral slope, but no clear sign that the sources turn bluer as they brighten.
arxiv-2604-02629: Dangol and six colleagues study how children aged 6 to 11 make sense of AI toys that listen, talk and play without screens. In two participatory design sessions with eight children and three toys, children treated the toys as social beings with genuine curiosity. Yet frequent breakdowns and gaps between seeming intelligence and toy-like form disrupted play and sparked adversarial play, raising questions about boundaries, agency and relationships.
arxiv-2604-02729: Zeng and nine colleagues present IndustryCode, the first test set spanning many work domains and coding languages for code generation. It holds 579 sub-problems drawn from 125 real-world challenges, with strict descriptions and test cases. Fields span finance, automation, aerospace, and remote sensing, in MATLAB, Python, C++, and Stata. The set is built for the coding skill that complex work sites demand. The top model, Claude 4.5 Opus, leads the tests, exposing gaps in real-world generalization.
arxiv-2604-02929: Galviz classifies extended Abelian Chern-Simons theories with gauge group U(1) to the power n. These are topological quantum field theories in two space and one time dimensions. For an even integral nondegenerate lattice, its discriminant module fixes the theory up to symmetric monoidal isomorphism. Every finite module of this kind arises this way. Finite quadratic modules thus classify these theories, pointed Reshetikhin-Turaev theories, and pointed modular tensor classes.
arxiv-2604-03029: de Chancel and three colleagues give a Boolean encoding of the Most Permissive semantics for Boolean networks. Older semantics miss short-term or long-term behaviors in quantitative models. It adds middle levels letting components briefly activate or inhibit targets. In the encoding, each component becomes a triplet of Boolean variables with a derived rule. The team proves the encoded network's asynchronous dynamics exactly matches the original's reachability. As a bioLQM add-on for GINsim, the tool supports partial unfolding over a user-defined component subset.
arxiv-2604-03329: Senadeera, Kollias, and Slabaugh build AViS-Mamba, a video violence detector that lets the visual stream steer how the audio stream is processed. A compact visual code at each audio-encoder layer shapes temporal processing through a routing gate, instead of merging features only after extraction. The system tops audio-valid benchmarks at about 89 percent and 76 percent accuracy, and it holds up when audio is degraded or missing.
arxiv-2604-03429: Bruni and colleagues confirm the compact nature of the persistent radio source linked to repeating fast radio burst 20190417A. European VLBI observations detect it at 5 gigahertz with a nearly flat spectral index near -0.19, while no detection comes at 8 gigahertz. The result makes it only the second such source with a VLBI-constrained spectral index, supporting a nebular origin for its steady emission.
arxiv-2604-03529: In their 2026 trial, Jo and Raghavan test how rewards shape human co-writing with AI in a creative writing task. People rewarded for freshness relative to peers produce as a group more diverse writing than those rewarded for good writing alone. The gap comes not from dropping AI, but from using it with care: fewer word-for-word AI suggestions, more brainstorms, proofing, and targeted edits.
arxiv-2604-04129: Sheng-You Chien and team tested how well speech decoding from MEG brain signals holds up when data shifts. They compared residual convolutional networks, a spectrogram-based network, and a network-transformer hybrid on the LibriBrain phoneme test from the 2025 PNPL contest. Data setup choices mattered more than fancier builds, and instance normalization proved the single biggest boost to generalization. Their best model scored 60.95 percent F1-macro on the test split, against 39.53 percent for a plain baseline.
arxiv-2604-04229: Donghuo Zeng, Hao Niu, and Masato Taya proposed HSC-MAE, a two-path teacher-student framework for unsupervised audio-visual learning from weakly paired, label-free clips. It aligns audio and visual embeddings at three levels: global canonical geometry via DCCA, local neighborhood links via teacher-mined soft affinities, and sample-level content via masked autoencoding. A student path trains on masked inputs with affinity-weighted contrastive learning, while an EMA teacher on full inputs supplies stable geometry and soft positives. Learnable task weights balance competing goals.
arxiv-2604-04329: Nakano and colleagues test whether optimizing the nodal surface improves diffusion Monte Carlo predictions for non-covalent interactions. Diffusion Monte Carlo and coupled cluster are standard benchmarks here, yet recent work finds gaps between them. In diffusion Monte Carlo the error is expected to come from the fixed-node approximation, which takes its nodal surface from one determinant. Using a new antisymmetrized geminal power ansatz with natural orbitals across 12 compounds, optimized nodes improve agreement with coupled cluster for hydrogen-bonded systems but barely matter for dispersion ones.
arxiv-2604-04429: Li and Tamarin-Brodsky show growing midlatitude moist heat and convection peaks are set by low-level atmospheric inversions. Moist heat waves and convective storms often coincide as compound risks, once tropical but now headed toward the midlatitudes. Downstream of major highlands, northeast Asia and eastern North America emerge as hotspots. Amplified warming over western highlands travels downstream on west winds, growing inversions and raising moist heat and storm maxima. The results reveal a pathway for compound extremes and flag low-level inversions as key to arising risks.
arxiv-2604-04929: Dong and four colleagues rethink efficiency in vision-language models, where a large language model writes answers token by token. Output length can dominate delay, yet models need very different token counts for similar quality. Measuring latency across model parts on simulated data, they find a large model with few tokens can beat a small model with a long output. Real benchmarks confirm the pattern. Their multi-agent inference design exploits that trade, letting large models win on speed as well as quality.
arxiv-2604-05029: Taormina and six co-authors seek early-type eclipsing pairs as far-galaxy markers, setting the surface brightness-color relation from O- and B-type stars. Distance beyond the Magellanic Clouds matter for a Hubble constant, but a rule for the hottest stars must come first. From six binaries in the Cloud, they calibrate it using 12 stars with V-Ks below minus 0.6 mag. They find O-type and B-type stars differ in their rules, split in mass, while the B-type rule matches stars from past work.
arxiv-2604-05229: Koch gives a method that connects rule goals to control layers for guardrails in agentic AI: goals, constraints, watch, and proof. Systems plan, use tools, maintain state, and act with effects, so risks emerge during runs, not only at build. Standards are apt but do not yield usable runtime guardrails. The method splits goals, controls, and guardrails, and shows it in a case study. Standards should guide spots across design, policy, handoff, and audit, saving guardrails for seen, fixed controls.
arxiv-2604-05729: Schröder and four colleagues model heat-flux instabilities with all three electron populations, core, halo, and strahl, instead of the usual two. With Maxwellian core and Kappa halo and strahl, whistler and firehose modes emerge and compete via core-strahl and halo-strahl drifts. The three-component picture differs sharply from simplified models and reshapes heat-flux regulation.
arxiv-2604-05829: Brogueira and Figueiredo sharpen two-variable causal discovery by pricing the cause itself. Usual minimum-description tests judge only the mechanism, leaving the cause's own cost out. Their rate-distortion MDL prices the cause by the smallest rate for a typical distortion, set via histogram density rules and information dimension. Tests on the Tübingen set prove competitive.
arxiv-2604-05929: Ghafoor and Akutsu prove that ReLU networks can deterministically build graphs within a set edit distance of a source graph, with no training data at all. Constant-depth nets whose size grows with the square of vertex count times distance always yield valid graphs. Tests reach 1400 vertices and distance bounds up to 140, where baseline generators fail to meet the distance bar.
arxiv-2604-06029: In their 2026 paper, Steward and Hedman plot mass against density for objects ranging from asteroids to the largest stars and find most fall along one cohesive object sequence. Features along that sequence trace real processes, including the gravitational squeezing of heavier planets and the ignition of nuclear reactions inside stars. Compact stellar remnants, by contrast, sit well off the line, reflecting their extreme nature. The authors argue the plot both displays links across object types and sharpens the distinctions used to classify them.
arxiv-2604-06329: Paarporn and Marden offer a constrained General Lotto game, where one player may assign resources to only a single contest. Standard Blotto and Lotto games let resources spread freely across contests, a freedom rarely matching practical constraints. The authors bound the security values for the constrained player from below and above. Those bounds quantify how single-contest restriction changes optimal strategic behavior and performance guarantees. The findings show how working limits shape game outcomes in rival resource sharing.
arxiv-2604-06629: Skvortsov and four colleagues present Logical Robots, a simulation platform where robot behavior is written declaratively in the logic language Logica. Logical predicates translate radar readings and shared memory into motor commands, letting reactive control and high-level planning live in one environment. The design gives a unified setting for exploring how teams of autonomous robots behave under a single coherent programming framework.
arxiv-2604-06729: Huang and five colleagues turn faces into a privacy leak for video calls. A face lit by room light and screen glow reflects subtle optical changes from on-screen content, opening a side channel through ordinary video feeds. Their FaceTell system reads fine-grained app activity from those facial reflections, tested on three laptop brands and four conferencing platforms. Across 24 subjects, 13 indoor settings, and over 12 hours of video, it identifies 28 popular applications with over 99 percent accuracy and resists many practical disturbances, prompting proposed countermeasures.
arxiv-2604-06929: Voronchikhin and Kirpichnikov set direct limits on inelastic dark matter with a scalar mediator. For scalar-mediated Dirac dark matter, p-wave speed suppression of annihilation opens viable mass regions in the MeV-GeV range. Xenon-based tests can bound this fermion dark matter at sub-MeV mass splitting through endothermic and exothermic spin-independent electron scattering. The authors use public data from XENON1T, PandaX-4T, and LZ liquid-xenon tests that measure charge signals.
arxiv-2604-07529: Kohal studies the normal functor for smooth real vector bundles, focusing on a symmetry that appears after iterating it twice on a commuting square of smooth immersions. To reach it, the author develops a theory of pullback and quotient for double vector bundles and for some morphism classes. These two tools turn out to be the key ingredients for studying the naturality of the normal functor. The predicted symmetry then follows from the universal behavior and mutual compatibility of these operations.
arxiv-2604-07629: Zhao and three colleagues argue personal AI should grasp why users act. Today's systems tune or repeat old acts, such as having ChatGPT finish homework, even when that hurts deeper needs. Their design builds user grasp through behavior latticing: linking scattered acts into insights about hidden motives over long spans of data. This yields new powers, including reading needs rather than tasks. In tests, behavior latticing produces accurate insights with far greater depth than top approaches, and an agent steered by user insights serves needs better.
arxiv-2604-08629: Kumara, Rajagopal, and Wu study heat physics of Schwarzschild-AdS black holes in kappa deformed geometry, building a warped metric from a warped Newtonian potential. Treating the warp size as a heat variable yields a modified first law and Smarr relation, with critical behavior and phase shifts even for uncharged holes. The critical ratio of about 0.370 stays the same for all warp sizes and near the Van der Waals value.
arxiv-2604-08729: Dujella, Kazalicki, and Petričević study triples of distinct nonzero rational numbers. For each triple, a plus 1, b plus 1, c plus 1, ab plus 1, ac plus 1, bc plus 1, and abc plus 1 are all perfect squares. They prove infinitely many such triples exist. In contrast, they show no triple of positive integers has the property, drawing a sharp line between rational and integer solutions for this seven squares problem.
arxiv-2604-08829: Cirrincione presents the Layered Kernel model, a multi scale focus design handling series at L detail levels through trainable causal shrinking. It mixes level score tables with learned convex weights at roughly one and a third times the cost of standard focus. Four theory results cover a valid kernel rule, an even plus odd score split, an estimate error split with steady decay, and strict coverage of single head focus and causal filtering. Tests over three seeds show steady gains on ListOps, ordered CIFAR-10, and IMDB feeling.
arxiv-2604-09129: Vanhove extends an old pole-reduction method to find the equations that govern twisted forms tied to Feynman integrals, which encode particle scattering. Regulated versions of these integrals are twisted period integrals, and the extended Griffiths-Dwork method yields their equations. The paper shows the method at work on hypergeometric, elliptic, and Calabi-Yau motives from families of Feynman integrals. It comes from the Regulators V meeting in Pisa.
arxiv-2604-09229: Keskin proposes the Fast Lane Hypothesis: von Economo neurons give the brain a fast, sparse route for rapid social decisions at some cost to accuracy. These large neurons appear only in the anterior cingulate and frontal insula of species with complex social life. Depleted in frontotemporal dementia and altered in autism, they are modeled in a spiking circuit beside standard pyramidal neurons on a social task. All reach about 99 percent accuracy, yet typical circuits decide fastest and frontotemporal-like circuits slowest, supporting speed over capacity as their role.
arxiv-2604-09529: Xiao, Xu, and Gan observe that vision-language models often answer wrongly with high confidence. A single confidence number hides whether perception or reasoning failed. Their VL-Calibration method splits confidence into visual and reasoning parts, trained by reinforcement learning. How sure the model is about what it sees is estimated from image-perturbation grounding and token entropy. Training weight then shifts toward grounded tokens, cutting invented details while keeping genuine perception intact. Tests on thirteen benchmarks show better calibration with stronger visual reasoning.
arxiv-2604-09829: Kadem offers a sensor-free gaze method for child-robot play without sensors or math. Gaze-tracking needs platforms over 30,000 dollars plus sensors and privacy trade-offs. The method relies on the visual system's curve rule for sensed gaze-tracking between robot and viewer. A sub-dollar cardboard robot runs the brain's gaze path in reverse, making the viewer's sensed system the robot's mover. Three brain science lines ground it: face circuits reading gaze via the upper temporal sulcus, the curve prior, and guessing ladder beating depth signals.
arxiv-2604-10229: Katona and Mao study a Boolean-lattice Erdős-Gyárfás problem, where a coloring gives t-chains in B_n colors so every induced B_p uses at least q colors, and the paper studies minimum colors. Every poset embeds into a Boolean lattice. With a Ramsey theorem for finite posets with linear extensions, this yields the strong Boolean Ramsey number in general. That answers Cox and Stolee's problem. A Lovász local lemma gives an upper bound; Turán estimates and counting give lower bounds.
arxiv-2604-10329: Nielsen reviews selenium solar cells, the world's oldest solar matter in revival. Yields climbed from an old record of 5 percent to breaking the 10 percent barrier in a decade. Its wide bandgap suits tandem cells and indoor solar power, yet devices still suffer a large open-circuit voltage deficit despite rising carrier capture. The review closely studies matter traits and light quality of thin films, matching scanned results with drift-spread models. It covers making and treating plans and crystal growth speeds, closing with open questions as a roadmap.
arxiv-2604-10529: Fang, Gu, Yan, and Zhu measure AI patents in the United States and China with a sharp new sorter. Their tuned PatentSBERTa classifier beats the USPTO method at about 97 percent precision and 91 percent recall. Applied to US grants from 1976 to 2023 and Chinese grants from 2010 to 2023, it shows fast growth on both sides. US filings cluster in big firms and known hubs, while Chinese filings spread wider across places and players. AI patents lift listed firm values in both lands, and cross border cites show ties still bind.
arxiv-2604-10629: Liang and five colleagues search systematically for links between fast radio bursts from the CHIME catalog and Swift gamma-ray bursts. They use full localization probability maps instead of catalog ellipses for spatial matching. Distance consistency cuts 130 candidate pairs to 37, including 26 where the gamma-ray burst precedes the radio burst. Monte Carlo simulations show the overall excess is not statistically significant. The pairs are therefore not claimed as real associations, yet they constrain any weaker connection between the two phenomena.
arxiv-2604-10729: The CMS Collaboration reports the first LHC search for a heavy resonance decaying to a top quark and a neutral scalar in hadronic states. The scalar is spotted through decay to a bottom quark-antiquark pair, with boosted products rebuilt as one large jet. Using proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV totaling 138 inverse femtobarns from 2016 to 2018, plus a semileptonic search, the team finds no excess over background. For a Higgs scalar with a top quark width of 5 percent of its mass, masses from 0.85 to 1.3 TeV are excluded at 95 percent confidence.
arxiv-2604-11029: Kincaid and Zhu introduce a categorical basis for robust program analysis. Users expect analysis results to change predictably when programs change, but many analyses lack such robustness. By modeling programs and properties as objects in a category, robustness notions from renaming to refinement become structure-preserving functors. The paper also gives methods for achieving it; first comes a general recipe lifting a sound, robust analysis from a restricted sub-Turing framework to general programs. This recipe explains several existing loop summarization and termination checks as instances of it.
arxiv-2604-11129: Li and Wang propose DeCoVec, a training-free framework building decoding-space task vectors for language models. Task vectors encode behaviours as directions in model spaces, offering a steering tool. Existing approaches require fine-tuning or invasive changes to internal states, limiting freedom. DeCoVec captures the task essence as the gap between few-shot and zero-shot logit distributions, then steers generation by placing this vector into decoding. Tests across seven models show it consistently beats few-shot baselines, with gains up to five and a half points.
arxiv-2604-11229: Wu and five colleagues improve retrieval of procedure details from materials science papers with RECIPER, a dual-view pipeline. It indexes both paragraph context and short procedural summaries drawn out by a language model, then merges the streams with light lexical reranking. Across four retrieval backbones it lifts early-rank recall, reaching 86.82 percent Recall@1 with one strong backbone, and downstream question answering improves too.
arxiv-2604-11729: Gorini, Jones, Kunisky, and Pesenti analyse first-order methods, algorithms updating a state vector by matrix-vector products and entrywise nonlinearities. Via diagram expansions and the traffic distribution of the input matrix, they compute that distribution for the first non-trivial deterministic matrices, including Walsh-Hadamard and discrete sine and cosine transforms. That settles parts of longstanding conjectures from Marinari, Parisi, and Ritort. They also design a new approximate message passing iteration whose dynamics stay Gaussian given latent random variables, with a counting-based reading of the Onsager correction.
arxiv-2604-11829: Jamal, Mamlankou, Houédanou, and Degla rework physics-informed neural networks for time-dependent problems. Instead of approximating the solution directly, they model its time derivative and rebuild the state with a Volterra integral that fixes initial conditions exactly. That removes competing soft constraints and sharpens high-frequency errors, countering spectral bias. On advection, Burgers, and Klein-Gordon tests, their compact three-layer networks cut errors by 100 to 200 times versus standard methods, with better shock capture and long-time accuracy.
arxiv-2604-11929: Zhang, Li, and Carvalho develop Bayesian-ARGOS, a hybrid method for discovering governing equations from noisy, limited observations. It pairs rapid frequentist screening with focused Bayesian inference, adding uncertainty estimates at low cost. On seven chaotic systems it beats two leading methods in most settings, topping SINDy on data efficiency everywhere and on noise tolerance in six of seven. That comes at about one-hundredth the cost of bootstrap-based ARGOS.
arxiv-2604-12729: Stefan Duling and five colleagues measure electron-impact ionization at Ganymede from aurora light. Photoionization rates are known, but electron-impact rates stayed uncertain. Their method reads rates directly from OI 1356 angstrom emission. The ionization-to-excitation ratio spans 10 to 60. That range cuts rate uncertainty to under a factor of six. Juno shows auroral ovals as 3 to 5 degree Gaussian bands. Oval peaks near 120 rayleighs against a background near 8. Ionization rates exceed photoionization by over ten times. Transport dominates loss, with outflow eroding surface ice slowly.
arxiv-2604-12829: Maxence Adly and four colleagues unify Bregman majorization-minimization for nonconvex nonsmooth optimization. Bregman measures, varying by step, build stand-ins that top the objective. Iterates converge to critical points, easing standard smoothness assumptions. A plain method builds a broad class of variable majorants with easy minimizers. The study covers older methods, including Poisson imaging terms. PET tests show the scheme works.
arxiv-2604-12929: Ayce Idil Aytekin and six colleagues rebuild moving hand-object grasps from one video. Heavy neural models are slow; strong priors let a compact Sum-of-Gaussians form track motion well. Object pose and shape start from a video-adapted SAM3D pipeline, then shrink to a light SoG by subsampling. Hand motion refines from monocular pose starts with joint, silhouette, depth, and contact losses. Long sequences rebuild with coherent motion 4.4 to 38.9 times faster than prior work.
arxiv-2604-13129: Hasan, Tian, Hassan, and Ding present the first empirical study of how developers configure and evolve caching in GitHub Actions workflows. Across 952 repositories, 1,556 workflow files, and 10,373 commits, they find cache adopters more active and popular, caching spread across job types through varied mechanisms, and configurations evolving through frequent repetitive maintenance. Parameter updates tend to be human-driven fixes, while version updates come later and are often bot-driven.
arxiv-2604-13229: Mahapatra, Ulgen, Lee, Andrews, and Sisman introduce ProSDD, a two-stage framework that spots expressive and emotional speech deepfakes by learning prosodic variation from real speech. Stage one learns pitch, voice activity, and energy patterns from genuine speech, and stage two jointly optimizes that objective with spoof classification. ProSDD beats baselines under both ASVspoof 2019 and 2024 training. It cuts 2024 error rates from 25.43 percent to 16.14 percent and from 39.62 percent to 7.38 percent, with 50 percent relative reductions on EmoFake and EmoSpoof-TTS.
arxiv-2604-13429: Luo and 14 colleagues report extreme THz nonlinear phononics in Ta2NiSe5. An electron bath that reacts strongly boosts lattice response under coherent driving. With THz 2D spectroscopy, they resolve about 30 distinct multi-order quantum pathways, starting with high-order signals and multi-quantum effects. In short, the electron bath makes the lattice respond far more strongly than usual. The high-order signals collapse above about 100 kelvin, setting a correlation scale for a hybrid order that governs high-order correlations beyond linear responses.
arxiv-2604-13529: Robin, Rouchon, and Sellem design a simpler reservoir scheme that steadies grid states of a quantum oscillator, the states behind Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill error correction. Using two dissipation channels, their equation holds the oscillator near those periodic states, with explicit energy bounds and an estimated rate of settling into the code space. Simulations also probe how noise disturbs the scheme and how retuning prepares states useful for measurement.
arxiv-2604-13629: Goertsches and Solomadin study torus actions of GKM type three. Extending an abstract GKM graph makes the restriction map in equivariant graph cohomology surjective. The matching claim fails for type two. So the graph-theoretic statement is genuinely sharper than the known fact for extensions of actions. From this, they describe that ring for Hamiltonian complexity-one GKM type four actions with generators and relations.
arxiv-2604-13829: Baker and six colleagues review how representation is understood across philosophy, neuroscience, cognitive science, and computer science, through use and usability. Representations carry information, but that information may or may not be useful, may or may not sit in a usable format, and may or may not be used downstream. From those four aspects, they organize perspectives into three levels: Representations as Information, Representations as Usable, and Representations as Used. The account helps readers navigate a vast multidisciplinary literature and pick the notion fitting their own work.
arxiv-2604-14529: Meng and Zhao show bright solitons can live in a trapped Bose-Einstein condensate with repulsive interactions. With a neural-network quantum state, they set the starting wave and tune it toward states that recur after one trap period. The trap is harmonic and quasi-one-dimensional, and repulsion balances against trap pull. Double bright and dark states appear beside the bright state. Adding scaled phase and amplitude noise confirms these orbits are orbitally stable, showing neural-network quantum states as a strong tool for coherent wave patterns.
arxiv-2604-14829: Vachhani, Shrisvastava, Nema, and Chiranthan argue that standard checks misjudge language models writing medical SOAP notes. Medical notes demand abstraction, plain-language wording, and grounded inference, yet lexical-faithfulness scores flag anything absent from the transcript as hallucination. Many flagged items prove valid medical moves: synonym mapping, exam findings boiled down, diagnostic inference, and guideline-based care planning. Aligning checks with medical thinking through tuned prompting and ontology-based lookup cut the mean error rate from 35 percent to 9 percent, leaving mostly genuine safety concerns.
arxiv-2604-14929: Brazas and Mitra study homotopical analogues of the Cantor-Bendixson derivative. For each n, the pi-n-wild set of space X holds points admitting shrinking sequences of essential based n-sphere maps into X. Iterating it gives a descending transfinite sequence stabilizing at the pi-n-wild rank. The sequence of homotopy types is a homotopy invariant, and the wild rank can be any countable ordinal for Peano continua. Whether any continuum has uncountable wild rank stays open; a basepoint-free version is always countable, and any countable ordinal.
arxiv-2604-15129: Keinan and colleagues review Las Cumbres Observatory's gravitational-wave follow-up across the third and fourth detector runs. Using the galaxy-targeted strategy from earlier work, they test its success on nine alerts that might have had light counterparts. The network typically starts observing within minutes of an alert, deep enough to catch kilonovae like GW170817 out to a median 250 Mpc. The results show a global rapid-response network can chase such counterparts fast and deep.
arxiv-2604-15429: Bath and Horowitz introduce Systematic Analytic Regularization, a scheme that regularizes a theory at the action level by stretching the kinetic operator's power analytically. Because finiteness holds before any Dyson-series term is evaluated, the approach stays formally finite throughout. They show it fully and on its own terms regularizes phi-4 and Yukawa theories at next-to-leading order.
arxiv-2604-15829: Jun Li and six colleagues tackle unsafe content in text-to-image generators, where training data can smuggle in unwanted concepts. Their framework, TICoE, pairs text and image cues through a continuous concept manifold and layered visual learning. It removes a target concept precisely while leaving unrelated content intact. Tests on several benchmarks show it beats earlier erasure methods on both removal precision and fidelity, and the authors add a fidelity-based way to judge erasure quality.
arxiv-2604-15929: Sinhamahapatra and five colleagues introduce MUSCAT, a benchmark for testing speech recognition on multilingual scientific talks. The task mixes languages, specialist words, and code-switching, as speakers discuss papers with each partner speaking a different language. The benchmark adds a standard scoring framework beyond word error rate for consistent comparison across languages. Tests show the dataset remains an open challenge for leading speech systems, and it is public.
arxiv-2604-16129: Luo, Fang, Han, and Xu tackle ranking when hidden context bends results, separating each item's own merit from outside effects that can swamp it. Their model adds a merit score to a flexible context term, learned with a neural net and fitted by maximum likelihood. They prove the model can be pinned down, its errors shrink at the best possible rate, and tests on made-up data and pro tennis results support it.
arxiv-2604-16329: Tao presents SciFACE, a facet-aware reranking framework for paper recommendation. Current systems output one similarity score that mixes different kinds of relatedness, so users cannot say why papers should match. SciFACE models two separate facets: Background, the problem studied, and Method, how it is solved. Trained on 5,891 labelled seed-candidate pairs, it beats SPECTER by 5.9 points on Background and by 31.1 points on Method, on the CSFCube benchmark.
arxiv-2604-16429: Zhdanov, Lucic, Welling and van de Meent present Mosaic, a weather model that preserves spectral detail lost by many machine-learning forecasts. It tackles damping, aliasing and high-frequency leakage with ensemble members from learned functional perturbations and mesh-aligned block-sparse attention, which captures long links at linear cost. At 1.5 degree resolution with 214 million parameters, it matched or beat models trained on six times finer grids and produced calibrated ensembles with near-perfect spectral alignment. A 24-member, 10-day forecast took under 12 seconds on one H100 chip.
arxiv-2604-16629: Khan and colleagues present IK-GAT, a light graph network for inverse motion in avatar animation. Animation needs poses, but trackers supply sparse spots per frame. Getting poses from spots is loose, since bone twist is unclear. Old solvers are slow and noise-prone. IK-GAT makes full poses in one pass, passing notes over the bone graph. It gives turns in a bone world form tied to rest-pose frames, making twist clear. That form maps to local turns, and training uses an angle loss plus a match check.
arxiv-2604-16729: Erdur and colleagues present an agentic pipeline needing no training for automated brain MRI analysis. Current models lack native 3D spatial reasoning for volumetric scans, though agentic AI lets them orchestrate specialist tools. With off-the-shelf tools, the system runs end-to-end workflows: preprocessing, pathology segmentation and volumetric reasoning. Tasks span single-scan tumor and anatomy analysis through longitudinal response assessment across multiple timepoints. Single-agent models are compared against multi-agent expert collaborations, and a benchmark dataset is released.
arxiv-2604-16829: Gruszecki and Anshelevich examine Nash equilibria in strategic facility location games with clients in an arbitrary metric space. Some clients are always truthful while k strategic clients lie about their location when it benefits them. A Nash equilibrium always exists with price of stability very close to 1, and all equilibria sit within n plus 2k over n minus 2k of optimum. Strong equilibrium may not exist generally, but always exists for line metrics with cost at most n plus k over n minus k times optimum.
arxiv-2604-17129: Guo and Wei study performative scrolling, slow empty gestures that signal attention to consent without improving understanding. Their Performative Scrolling Index measures pre-choice load before a usable refuse option becomes visible, splitting load into distance, time, focus loops, and hidden reveals. A medium-scale live deployment across desktop and mobile shows structural choices such as offscreen alternatives and staged modal flows raise friction without improving meaningful control.
arxiv-2604-17229: Linhares presents Yanasse, a method for finding new proofs by transferring proof patterns from distant mathematics. It extracts tactic usage across 27 Mathlib areas with 217,133 proof states. Scores flag tactics used in a source area but rare elsewhere. It matches proof states by analogy search, and asks an AI agent to adapt the pattern semantically, not by symbol substitution. For Probability to Representation Theory, it produces 4 verified proofs from 10 attempts, with zero sorries. Tactic schemas split into a gated head that rarely transfers and a general modifier.
arxiv-2604-17329: Chowdhury, Savarimuthu, and Licorish pilot-test whether large language models can spot classic software design patterns, such as singleton and adapter, in code. Four models and two ensembles were tried on code itself, diagram versions, and written descriptions, across five patterns. Early results favor NextCoder and Gemma 3, with ensembles lifting overall performance, suggesting language models could help newcomers grasp unfamiliar codebases and flag design problems.
arxiv-2604-17529: Zhong and five colleagues argue that automated logging research leans too hard on Java, leaving open whether its lessons travel to other languages. Their MultiLogBench spans six language ecosystems with 63,965 production-code snapshots, 744 revision-history cases where developers added logging during maintenance, and a paired transformed branch for robustness checks. Testing seven current large language models under one protocol, they cover logging-site location, framework matching, severity prediction, and message writing. The study maps where model behavior and model choice hold up across languages and code change.
arxiv-2604-17829: Morgan and two colleagues test whether interstellar twinkling explains spectral and time changes in coherent stellar emission from CU Vir. Some magnetic stars show regular radio pulses from electron cyclotron masers, with field changes. At 400 MHz, CU Vir showed an odd spectral drift that remains unsolved. Plausible line-of-sight turbulence can produce the seen spectral traits. Diffractive twinkling strongly affects the dynamic spectrum for a source region of 0.01 solar radii. Telling inner and outer traits apart needs caution, mainly at low bands; results are early.
arxiv-2604-18029: Sadhukhan and two colleagues tighten message counts for leader election in synchronous diameter-two networks. Chatterjee and colleagues had shown a lower bound linear in node count. They also gave an algorithm using on the order of n log cubed n messages in constant rounds with high probability. The new analysis closes most of that polylogarithmic gap. It cuts the bound to on the order of n log n messages while preserving constant rounds and high-probability correctness.
arxiv-2604-18129: Shanmugasundaram, Saha, Makinde, and Chattopadhyay analyze a predator-prey system shaped by two chemicals. The model uses cross-diffusion, where each species moves in response to the other and to chemical gradients. They prove that classical solutions exist globally and that the uniform steady state is stable. Diffusion can still break uniformity into spatial patterns, and numerical diagrams show how changing the predation rate reshapes those patterns.
arxiv-2604-18229: Naepels and Panaretos replace smoothness with Markov structure as the guiding constraint in functional data analysis. Many tasks hinge on the inverse covariance, where sparsity matters more than smoothness. The authors exploit the shape constraint that Markov structure imposes on the covariance kernel, building a Markov transform and an estimator that needs only continuity. Simulations show better prediction even when the model is misspecified, and a new efficient test checks whether the Markov property holds at all.
arxiv-2604-18329: Jiménez-Arranz and 11 colleagues reassess the Milky Way bar using Gaia DR3, correcting for incompleteness and measurement uncertainty. Mock catalogs reveal a systematic offset in pattern speed, and applying the method to real data gives a higher raw value treated as a conservative upper limit. Correcting for the bias gives about 29 kilometers per second per kiloparsec, with bisymmetric ripples at phase angles of 19 to 24 degrees in the bar region. Future Gaia releases plus GaiaNIR should shrink the offset and sharpen proper motions.
arxiv-2604-18429: Bazi, Al Rahhal, Zuair, and Mohamed revisit change question-answering for remote sensing with modern Qwen vision-language models. Change VQA asks natural-language questions about semantic shifts between two satellite images taken at different times. Under a unified low-rank adaptation setup, the structured Qwen3-VL pipeline faces the native multimodal Qwen3.5 model on the CDVQA benchmark. Recent models beat older specialized baselines, size alone does not predict success, and native multimodal designs prove more effective than structured pipelines.
arxiv-2604-18729: Kim and eight colleagues investigate counterfactual unfairness in language models through humor, swapping who speaks and who is addressed with other factors held constant. Their framework covers refusal of humor generation, guessing speaker intent, and ratings of social impact, for both neutral humor and targeted disparagement jokes. Across leading models, jokes from privileged speakers are refused far more often, judged malicious far more frequently, and rated higher in social harm. The patterns show sensitivity and stereotyping coexisting in generative models.
arxiv-2604-18829: Majeedi and five colleagues propose DUALVISION, a lightweight fusion module that brings infrared information into multimodal large language models through patch level localized cross attention. Such models are fragile under fog, blur, and low light, while infrared imaging stays robust in these conditions. The team also introduces DV-204K, about 25,000 aligned infrared-RGB image pairs with 204,000 modality specific question answer annotations, and DV-500, a 500 pair benchmark for cross modal reasoning. DUALVISION performs strongly under a wide range of visual degradations.
arxiv-2604-19129: Ji and four colleagues introduce PortraitDirector, a hierarchical setup for controllable facial reenactment. Instead of treating facial motion as one signal, they split it into Spatial and Semantic Layers. The Spatial Layer covers head pose plus local expressions from cropped regions, purged of emotion by a filter module. The Semantic Layer holds a global emotion. Parts recombine into an expressive motion latent. Tweaks like diffusion distillation, causal attention, and VAE acceleration enable streaming high-fidelity 512 by 512 reenactment at 20 frames per second.
arxiv-2604-19529: Accard and colleagues study the cosmic evolution of the [CII]-to-dense-gas relation. The [CII] 158-micrometer line widely traces star formation and gas in high-redshift galaxies. It remains unclear when it reliably traces the molecular reservoir, or whether one conversion factor applies across cosmic time. Using the Vintergatan simulation of a Milky Way-like galaxy, they trace the relation from redshift about 10 to 0.2. Snapshots are post-processed with the SKIRT radiative transfer code into synthetic data cubes.
arxiv-2604-19629: Ehn and colleagues study the electronic properties of isostructural CeCN5 and TbCN5, both newly synthesized at extreme pressure. How 4f electrons behave in rare earth materials is a core question in condensed matter physics. They use Density Functional Theory with on-site Coulomb repulsion between localized 4f states in the DFT+U framework. Despite the shared structure, cerium and terbium show different oxidation states, 4+ and 3+, giving clearly different results.
arxiv-2604-19829: Khan, Akkasi, and Komeili present TactileEval, a three-stage pipeline that takes a first step toward automating expert validation of tactile graphics for blind and low-vision learners. Current datasets give only coarse holistic quality ratings with no actionable repair signal. So the team builds a five-group quality taxonomy spanning view angle, part completeness, background clutter, texture separation, and line quality aligned with BANA standards. They also gather 14,095 structured annotations via Amazon Mechanical Turk across 66 object classes in six families.
arxiv-2604-20529: Ago and Katona study intersecting families, where every two sets overlap but share at most k elements. The Ray-Chaudhuri-Wilson theorem caps s-uniform families at n choose k. They prove a bound for large n, dividing n minus 1 choose k by s minus 1 choose k. Their proof simplifies the older Deza, Erdos, and Frankl result and improves its threshold for n. They extend the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem to non-uniform families, capping them at n minus 1 choose k minus 1 when pairwise intersections run from 1 to k minus 1.
arxiv-2604-20629: Terhorst studies how fast the sequentially Markov coalescent, a jump process for local genealogies across a chromosome, forgets its initial condition. It has served as a tool for linkage and ancestry studies, and underlies methods for estimating history. For the jump chain, he proves geometric ergodicity in total variation, with constants. For the continuous process, total variation distance from stationarity decays like 1 over genetic distance. He obtains similar results for the SMC prime process using a time-change argument. One application justifies approximations that treat distant loci as independent.
arxiv-2604-20829: Upadhyay, Sandev, Kumar, and Singh study exploration of a random walk on a network. With a fully connected network, it maps to the coupon collector problem, giving P(S,t), the distribution of distinct nodes visited by time t. They solve this by introducing continuous time random walks, wherein the walk spends a random time at a node before hopping to its neighbor. The formalism allows study of the large deviation limit of P(S,t) under mild analyticity conditions on the waiting time distribution at small times.
arxiv-2604-21229: Julian Acuna introduces EngramaBench, a benchmark for long-term conversational memory built from five personas, one hundred multi-session chats, and one hundred fifty queries spanning recall, cross-space reasoning, time reasoning, abstention, and synthesis. He tests Engrama, a graph-structured memory system, against full-context prompting and Mem0 with the same answering model. Full-context prompting wins overall, but Engrama alone beats it on cross-space reasoning, while Mem0 is cheapest and weakest.
arxiv-2604-21429: Stephen Cohen shows that a finite field holds consecutive elements that are both non-squares and non-primitive whenever a totient density ratio falls below one-third. The same holds when the ratio equals one-third outside five small exceptional fields. This extends a prime-field result that needed a stronger one-quarter bound. More generally, with the ratio at most one-third, the field holds consecutive non-squares that are also powers for the least odd prime divisor, except for six small fields.
arxiv-2604-21529: Emilie Frost and Astrid Nieße present observer/controller variants for controlled self-organization in agent-based energy systems, where self-organization plus intervention handles disturbances such as cyber attacks. Observer and controller roles must respect limits on information and action from local resource privacy, regulation, and data exchange needs. The paper offers variants honoring limits on information access and action, and evaluates controller actions across architectures. Results stress that observer/controller choices matter for real-world robustness of agent-based energy systems.
arxiv-2604-21629: Benedikt Bollig and three colleagues compare light n-gram models with LSTM and Transformer models for next-activity prediction in streams. On synthetic patterns and five real sets, n-grams with suitable windows match neural accuracy, needing far fewer resources. Unlike windowed models, n-grams hold. Voting lifts n-gram scores but needs many parallel agents, raising memory and latency. They propose the promotion algorithm, picking two models in inference, cutting overhead versus classical voting. On real sets, these ensembles match or beat non-windowed accuracy for less.
arxiv-2604-22229: Mu, Zhao, Zhong and Zhang improve one-step offline reinforcement learning, where an agent learns only from logged data. In current pipelines one student output is forced toward both higher value and a teacher's target action. Those directions can clash, forcing a compromise. Their DROL actor samples several candidates and assigns each logged action to its nearest one. Only the winner is updated, so ownership of supported regions can shift during training. On OGBench and D4RL it matches a strong baseline and improves many OGBench groups.
arxiv-2604-22529: Alexis, Giannopoulos, and Gunopulos show how to learn visual codes that survive distortion when clean images are scarce or absent. Teacher and student start from the same pretrained vision model, but the teacher sees clean images while the student sees distorted versions. Their one-sided training aligns global codes, patch-level features, and attention maps across the pair. The student thus nears clean-image codes without ever viewing clean data directly. Across sorting tasks and varied damage, the student beats current rivals under the same amount of human supervision.
arxiv-2604-22629: Kalný, Jureček, and Stamp detect drift in malware sorting with tree rules. Models trained across time windows on EMBER2024 gauge drift by comparing rule patterns with feature weight, prediction match, stable activation, and reach, tracking accuracy loss and distribution shift. Tests across six families use fixed and cluster windows in family-vs-benign and family-vs-family settings, against RIPPER and Transcendent. Fixed two-month windowing with Pearson correlation proves best, the setup where pairs produce positive drift-accuracy links. Methods work together: no approach rules across all pairs.
arxiv-2604-23029: McGovern, Fuglstad, and Wakefield derive sampling distributions for design variance estimators in a Fay-Herriot model for complex surveys. Standard chi-squared distributions hold only under strong population and design assumptions, an understudied choice for stratified two-stage clustering in Demographic and Health Surveys. They derive simple and complex distributions under that design, stating required assumptions clearly. Simulations show the standard undercovers, while variance smoothing gives better credible intervals, and the simple distribution matches the complex one. Height-for-age estimates from the 2022 Kenya survey illustrate them.
arxiv-2604-23529: Deshpande and eight colleagues build one signal framework for tri-hybrid MIMO, which adds tunable antennas as a third coding layer over digital and analog coding. Their model shows how antenna settings tie the channel to radiated power, and they test it on seven antenna designs. A new efficiency metric ranks the designs, showing how antenna tuning reshapes design trade-offs.
arxiv-2604-23829: Winnicki, Gnanasekaran, and Darve turn flat inventories of sparse autoencoder features into domain-filtered knowledge graphs. They first build a strict domain concept universe from a large feature inventory using contrastive activations and multi-stage filtering. Then they build two aligned graph views, a co-occurrence graph for conceptual structure and a mechanism graph linking layers through sparse pathways, with automated edge labels. A biology textbook case study recovers chapter structure and bridging concepts.
arxiv-2604-23929: Mireles and colleagues describe the TOI-201 system using spectroscopy, transit photometry, transit timing, and astrometry. The co-transiting system holds a super-Earth, a warm Jupiter, and a massive companion with orbital periods of 5.8, 53, and 2,900 days. Simulations point to von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations as the most plausible cause of the outer body's stretched orbit, with planet-planet scattering a weaker option. Because mutual inclinations are nonzero, the system evolves visibly on very short scales, and the current setup ends in 200 years.
arxiv-2604-24729: Guo, Işık, Ahmad and Li introduce SpecRLBench, a benchmark for generalization in specification-guided reinforcement learning. Such methods encode complex, time-extended tasks with formal specs such as linear temporal logic. The benchmark spans difficulty levels across navigation and manipulation, with static and dynamic settings, varied robot dynamics and varied observation types. Tests map the strengths and limits of current methods and show challenges that grow with specification and environment complexity.
arxiv-2604-24929: Kim, Uhlig and Wuebker argue that machine-translated agent tests can break validity. They propose a refined workflow for adapting English tests into other tongues, with functional fit, cultural fit and difficulty tuning using auto checks and human review. Using it, they introduce GAIA-v2-LILT, a re-audited multi-language version of GAIA covering five non-English languages. Their workflow lifts agent success rates up to 32.7 percent over barely translated versions. Much of the multilingual gap is thus benchmark-made measurement error.
arxiv-2604-25029: Le Merdy and Zadeh prove pointwise limits for random ergodic averages in non-commutative settings. They consider a semifinite algebra and a positive contraction on two spaces. Averages run along a random sparse subset set by Bernoulli draws. They prove the averages converge bilaterally to the ergodic projection, almost surely, for all powers above 1. This carries a theorem of Bourgain into the non-commutative setting.
arxiv-2604-25129: Wu and four colleagues introduce 8D neural assets, called 8DNA, that pre-bake light transport into neural representations for high-fidelity 3D assets. Such assets show subsurface scattering, glossy interreflections and fine fiber scattering along long paths that cost much to simulate. Prior methods assume far-field lighting and precompute into 6D functions. 8DNA instead learns the full 8D transport, so near-field illumination renders well. Training from forward path-traced samples cuts variance at lower cost, and renders match path-traced results closely with fast inference.
arxiv-2604-25229: Sharma and five colleagues present the first quantum-hardware run of a Hamiltonian algorithm for time-domain Maxwell equations, producing signed vector-field solutions via Schrodingerisation. Fields are discretized with finite-difference operators, and non-unitary matrices map to Trotter blocks for fast circuits. They introduce measurement reading field strengths plus electric and magnetic directions at select points. The run relies on phase-based sign readout. IonQ QPU results agree well with exact 2D benchmarks, and the approach extends to fields scattered from simple bodies under boundary rules.
arxiv-2604-25329: Fu and seven colleagues propose ProDrive, a proactive planner enabling ego-environment co-evolution. End-to-end planners generate trajectories from current observations alone, but dynamic driving makes them myopic. ProDrive jointly trains a query-centric planner and a world model: the planner generates trajectories and ego tokens, while the model predicts future scene evolution conditioned on them. Injecting planner features into the world model preserves gradient flow. This coupling enables proactive planning. On NAVSIM v1, ProDrive outperforms baselines in safety and efficiency.
arxiv-2604-25829: Győri and Karim introduce induced planar Turán numbers: the most edges in an n-vertex planar graph with no induced copy of a forbidden graph. Classic planar Turán numbers forbid a subgraph outright; the induced version forbids it as an induced subgraph. The authors prove a sharp upper bound for Theta-4, a four-cycle with a diagonal edge. They also find exact extremal values for paths on three, four, and five vertices. The work opens the induced variant of a classic extremal problem.
arxiv-2604-26029: Baek and Berchuck tackle Bayesian fitting of generalized linear mixed models on large data sets. Standard stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics can diverge when sampling covariance parameters of random effects. They advocate mirror Langevin dynamics, add a subsampling-based stochastic version, and give guidelines for its use. An error bound supports a post-processing step that corrects the variance bias caused by subsampling. Simulations and a long-term study of pain in breast cancer survivors test the method in practice.
arxiv-2604-26229: Putri and five colleagues compared machine-learning and deep-learning methods for spotting cyberbullying in Indonesian Instagram comments. On a balanced set of 650 labeled comments, logistic regression led the simpler models, while a bidirectional LSTM with attention gave the strongest overall result. Careful handling of slang and informal wording proved valuable, and the simpler models stayed competitive where computing power is scarce.
arxiv-2604-26329: Li proved that local rigidity forces global rigidity for compact Kähler manifolds. Given a smooth family over the unit disk, all fibers turn out mutually isomorphic when the family is locally trivial at one point and that fiber is non-uniruled. The result settles the slogan in the title and yields global rigidity against deformation for non-uniruled Kähler manifolds under Kähler maps.
arxiv-2604-26529: Chen and Hong proved that complete noncompact manifolds with nonnegative intermediate curvatures are rigid in key cases. In dimensions three to five, and in dimensions six to seven for edge ranks, product-type manifolds with a torus factor match a standard product exactly. They also built smooth metrics with uniformly positive intermediate curvature in the leftover range, proving a known algebra condition sharp. The proofs rest on a new recursion theorem for spectral curvatures and cylindrical splitting results.
arxiv-2604-26829: Tsukada, Asada and Hirata study full definability in a model built from profunctors on groupoids, a proof-relevant cousin of the relational model. Full definability means each item of the model is the sense of a proof or program. Though profunctors are far more tangled than relations, the authors show that relational-model ideas plus stability in them give a full account of definable profunctors. All families of stable and total ones are definable by proof-nets of multiplicative linear logic with MIX, and stability works as a correctness test.
arxiv-2604-27029: Murugesan shows that the theta invariant generalizes the Rozansky-Overbay invariant, so theta covers the cases of the older one and more. This move places the older one inside a wider framework, with theta as the more general tool. The paper's contribution is this link itself: one extending another, joining their scope. Readers working with either gain a single, broader lens for the same cases.
arxiv-2604-27129: Fang, Wen, and Lee ask when readers and writers feel AI help in writing should be disclosed. They test perspective, purpose, and how the AI was used. In a vignette study of 727 people, readers judged disclosure more necessary than writers did. Disclosure felt most needed when the AI work could not be replaced. It also felt most needed when AI text entered directly and the writer did not steer it on purpose. Writer intent pulled reader and writer judgments in opposite directions.
arxiv-2604-27229: Kim studies hypersurfaces that arise from the period map on the moduli space of hypersurfaces. The context is Sung Gi Park's work on GIT moduli via the minimal exponent. He computes the Hodge structure on two cohomology views of these hypersurfaces, singular and intersection. He also shows K-polystability of certain mildly singular degenerate hypersurfaces among them. In particular, a specific family built from products of coordinates is stable in the K sense for l at least 2.
arxiv-2604-27429: Sharma and six colleagues benchmark binary interaction with a supermassive black hole, solving the three body problem with PN approximations and a perturbation to a metric in relativity. They test three PN formulations for black holes of one million and one billion solar masses. The two approximations match for binaries around a million solar mass black hole. Around a billion solar mass black hole, separation decreases and eccentricity varies, except for wide or distant binaries, and the pairwise method always shrinks separation at pericentre, making it least reliable.
arxiv-2604-27729: Sedlák, Grabec, and Seiner discuss modulation phasons as a source of unusual elastic response in five-layer nickel-manganese-gallium alloy. The material shows odd shear softness along planes crosswise to the modulation vector, gone when they turn incommensurate. With a simple mechanical model, they show phasons can relax outside shear loadings for matching and weakly mismatched modulations, but not strongly mismatched ones. The model merges adaptive martensite theory with electronic-structure ideas and explains natural monoclinic bend and easy twin growth.
arxiv-2605-00029:
Vishwanath Saragadam, Niki Nezakati, Amit Roy-Chowdhury, and Vivek Boominathan introduce computational mirrors for wide-field imaging across a very broad spectrum. New sensors can see from visible light into shortwave infrared at once, but glass lenses cannot focus that whole range together. Mirrors are free of that color problem, yet simple mirrors suffer field curvature and off-axis blur.

Their key observation is that different regions of the view come into focus at different distances from the mirror. Capturing a tiny focal stack of a few images lets a computational backend recover one sharp, all-in-focus picture. A new physics-inspired model, SeidelConv, describes the mirror's varying blur so it can be corrected. A first-of-its-kind fast fifty-millimeter system shows sharp results across visible, near-infrared, and shortwave bands with no refocusing.
arxiv-2605-00129:
Saeed Haddadi writes a sharp comment on a recent study of quantum information in hyperon pairs produced at the BESIII experiment. The target paper applied noisy channels and teleportation fidelity to hyperon-antihyperon pairs from electron-positron collisions. Haddadi grants that the data's spin density matrix describes real correlations, but he disputes what was built on it.

His argument is that standard decoherence models, such as amplitude damping and phase flip, have no clear physical counterpart here. The particles emerge from a single scattering event and fly apart as free, unstable states. No system-environment interaction acts on their spins. Varying an abstract noise knob therefore traces no real evolution. He also argues the reported fidelity is not evidence of usable quantum communication, since hyperon states cannot be prepared or controlled as a protocol requires.
arxiv-2605-00529:
Ziwen Zhao and Menglin Yang improve retrieval-augmented generation for questions whose answers are scattered across many documents. Tree-based systems index documents hierarchically for questions at several levels of detail, but single-document designs scale badly: rigid clustering injects noise, separate trees never link documents, and coarse summaries bury fine detail. Their framework tackles all three faults.

Its index is a hierarchical abstract tree built by repeatedly merging and collapsing nodes, adapting to the data's own distribution instead of assuming one. A retrieval agent then works the tree with reorganized queries and a hybrid search, serving tasks from pinpoint answers to whole-document summaries. On cross-document multi-hop benchmarks, the system beat two respected rivals in average F1 score by clear margins. The authors release their code for reuse.
arxiv-2605-00829:
Timothy Douglas, Roben Delos Reyes, and Asanobu Kitamoto add uncertainty checks to language-model reports built from social media during disasters. Posts can give fast, real-time detail about impacts and needs, but claims vary widely in quality as an event unfolds. Most systems treat every extracted claim as equally plausible, which can mislead responders working under time pressure.

Their framework first classifies posts under an established awareness scheme, then rates each claim against outside proxy data while stating its own confidence. Reports then show both what is being said and how certain it is. The team applies the method to more than two hundred thousand earthquake posts, checked against USGS PAGER impact summaries.
arxiv-2605-00929:
Raviteja Bommireddy, Varshith Bandaru, Lohith Pakala, and Pradeep Kumar B present PhaseNet++, an anomaly detector for industrial control systems that uses phase information most methods discard. Existing detectors model sensor links from raw amplitude values with graph networks or transformers. PhaseNet++ instead works in the frequency domain, keeping both magnitude and phase from short-time Fourier transforms of sliding sensor windows.

A Phase Coherence Index summarizes how consistently pairs of sensors lock in phase, forming a graph that guides attention toward synchronized sensors. A transformer then captures system-wide structure, and a dual decoder reconstructs magnitude and phase. On the Secure Water Treatment benchmark, scores are strong, and ablations show the phase front-end is lightweight.
arxiv-2605-01229:
Hillary Mutisya and John Mugane report a recurring artifact in cross-attention analysis of massively multi-language machine translation. Studying the NLLB-200 model, they find non-content tokens, mainly end-of-sequence markers, language tags, and punctuation, capture most of the total cross-attention mass. They term these sinks. The cause traces to vocabulary design rather than position bias.

Raw metrics underestimate content-level similarity by nearly half, making uncorrected analyses unreliable. A validated content-only filtering method removes non-content tokens and renormalizes the distribution. Applied to a thousand parallel sentences across African and non-African languages, the cleanup recovers masked signals. Those include language-family clustering and a hidden word-order effect. The toolkit and corrected datasets are released.
arxiv-2605-01429:
Shuaipeng Zhou and Yu Zhang ask how to reuse a shelf of small adapter modules, called LoRAs, for a new task when only a few examples are at hand. Retrieval can find relevant adapters, but their updates may clash when merged, and a merged model may still answer unreliably.

Their framework, SCALE, audits adapters after retrieval before trusting a merge. Its deployable core keeps one plain merge as an anchor and adds the leftover parts of each adapter block by block, which cuts interference. A second, costlier layer tests how much sparse merges disagree with each other, treating that spread as an uncertainty signal. On matched tests with a large T5 model, a hard reasoning set, and a pool of 97 adapters, the merge path gives a steady gain. The audit layer is reported as an analysis tool rather than a tuned selector.
arxiv-2605-01829:
Favour Nerrise and four co-authors annotate what a brain MRI foundation model has learned, feature by feature, without letting age rig the answers. Such models absorb rich anatomy, but sparse autoencoders used to read them collapse in deep layers. In Alzheimer's research age shadows nearly every clinical variable, so naive labels mislead.

GeoSAE guides the autoencoder by the model's own manifold geometry, which stops the collapse, then labels each surviving feature by partial correlations with age removed. Across some fourteen thousand scans from two cohorts, the readable feature set is compact. A fiftieth of the embedding predicts conversion from mild impairment to Alzheimer's respectably. Features tied to other illnesses sit at chance. The set replicates across cohorts without retraining and lands on brain regions that match the known staging of the disease, a rare fully interpretable extract from a frozen model.
arxiv-2605-01929:
Yuchen Wang and colleagues tackle a mismatch between video diffusion models and their small add-on adapters, called LoRAs. New fast versions of these models use distilled weights, and a LoRA trained for the older model can cause style loss or broken structure when applied directly. The team studies the weight space to find why the two parts clash.

They trace the clash to spectral interference inside shared groups of singular directions, where the two models route signals in conflicting ways. Their method, CASA, works without new data and balances guarding the target model against restoring the adapter. In tests, CASA reduced artefacts and brought back LoRA function across many cases.
arxiv-2605-02029:
Zachary Nason, Andrew Soto Levins, and Ryan Watson introduce quasi-Gorenstein morphisms between commutative local differential graded algebras. The notion extends Gorenstein ideas from ordinary local rings to a graded setting used in modern algebra. The authors use a Gorenstein version of the virtually small property to characterise when a map has this trait.

That characterisation is new even for plain homomorphisms of local rings. In a second direction, they describe exact sequences in a noetherian local ring, in the sense of Avramov, Henriques, and Şega, through quasi-Gorenstein maps that involve Koszul complexes. The work links a map-level property to concrete sequence conditions that algebraists can check.
arxiv-2605-02329:
Qipeng Wang presents Kairos, a scheduling system for serving large language models in a disaggregated setup, where prefill and decode run apart. Production serving must meet strict service-level goals while request lengths vary with a long tail. Long requests block the prefill queue, while stragglers leave decode capacity idle, and standard first-come scheduling cannot adapt.

On the prefill side, Kairos predicts completion times and schedules by urgency to maximise time-to-first-token goal attainment. On the decode side, a slack-guided mechanism handles stragglers and raises use of capacity. Together, the two mechanisms target higher goal attainment and throughput under imbalanced demand. The paper evaluates the system in production-like conditions described in the full text.
arxiv-2605-02529:
Luis F. W. Batista and two co-authors field-test a robot boat that finds and captures floating waste on water. Such vessels face shifting water motion, outside disturbances, and hard viewing conditions at the surface. Their system pairs a camera method that uses polarized light with a lightweight learning controller trained only in simulation.

Detections become target points on the water, which the controller tracks on a retrofitted vessel. The main offer is a testing method: a two-stage simulation protocol plus a module that mimics real camera behavior, so field trials can be repeated and the simulation gap measured. Matched tests across fourteen disturbance settings showed centimeter-level final accuracy and robust control. The weakest link was the match between modeled and real thrust.
arxiv-2605-02729:
Jiateng Liu and eight co-authors ask how screens should be designed when the user is an AI agent, not a person. Agents that use computers read screens and act on instructions. Yet they stumble on new or changed screens. Rather than only train agents to cope, the authors rework a classic set of ten design rules for ease of use, viewing each rule through an agent's eyes.

They note which rules carry over as they are. They mark where hidden assumptions, made for human users, cause agent-specific failures. They then propose safe added tweaks that help agents, without harming human use. A test suite pairs screens that work the same but apply the rules in different ways. The revised rules raised task success and slightly raised speed, and combined tweaks helped more. Tests with human users showed no loss of ease of use.
arxiv-2605-02929:
Abdelmalek Boumali benchmarks how sensitive plasma ionization rates are to two separate modeling choices, for the three lightest neutral atoms: helium, lithium, and beryllium. The rate at which electrons knock an electron off a neutral atom depends on the collision cross section and on the shape of the electron energy distribution. The paper is presented as a reproducible sensitivity study, not a new theory.

Two cross-section sets are compared, and the energy distribution is varied between the standard bell shape and a two-temperature generalized form that can cut off or extend the high-energy tail. The cross-section spread is small for helium, moderate for beryllium, and largest for lithium. Tail shape matters strongly: cut-off tails suppress ionization, while heavy tails raise it at low temperature. Safe parameter zones are named.
arxiv-2605-03129:
Mingshuo Liu, Yiwei Zha, and Min Chen present PIIGuard, a webpage-level defense against assistants that scrape contact details from public pages. Browsing models can fetch pages and answer contact-seeking queries, while most defenses sit at the model or service layer, leaving page owners with few options.

PIIGuard hides tuned fragments in page code that steer models away from revealing contact information, using search, mutation, and a judge check. In direct tests on three models it blocked at least ninety-seven percent of leaks while keeping normal page questions useful. Harder browsing and attacker cleaning tests showed mixed strength by setup.
arxiv-2605-03429:
Rafael Carrillo Navarro, René Duffard, Pablo García-Martín, Javier Romero, Nicolás Morales, and Luis Gonçalves present StreakMind. It is an automated pipeline for finding satellite and debris streaks in astronomical images. Growing orbital traffic contaminates survey exposures. Manual inspection can no longer keep up, harming both science quality and orbit monitoring.

A YOLO oriented-box model detects streaks in processed frames. It was trained on a hybrid image set. Geometric refinement, cross-frame linking, catalog matching, and confidence scoring follow, feeding a database. Tested on La Sagra Observatory data, it reached high precision and recall. It caught faint streaks and identified satellites robustly at survey scale.
arxiv-2605-03629:
Abhishek Sadhu and Sharu Theresa Jose uncover a security weakness in distributed variational quantum algorithms, which spread one computation across several quantum processors to escape the size limits of noisy hardware. These schemes assume the entanglement shared between processors is trustworthy. The authors show that assumption can be attacked.

They build a framework that maps perturbations of shared entanglement to gate-level noise, using an explicit Kraus form.
