The authors argue that patient-reported measures should be routine in counseling and follow-up.
pmc-13298129:
Hannah Brown and Sharon E. Clarke review shortened MRI protocols for cancer detection and surveillance, in a 2026 narrative survey. Full scans can be long, costly, and hard to access, so abbreviated versions aim to keep accuracy while cutting time. Three settings receive attention: prostate cancer, pancreatic cyst monitoring, and liver cancer surveillance.

Across selected patients, abbreviated scans may match full examinations, and wider use could improve access. Evidence gaps remain, including weak study design in places and little long-term follow-up. The authors favour a risk-adapted pattern, reserving full scans for higher-risk situations, and they call for prospective studies before routine adoption widens.
pmc-13298329:
Babar Azeem and KuZilati KuShaari review how fertiliser carriers made from polysaccharide hydrogels should be tested, in a 2026 engineering survey. Moisture, acidity, ionic strength, and microbial activity all reshape release through coupled effects. The authors propose a soil-based testing plan and better forecast models so designs can scale from laboratory promise toward dependable field performance.
pmc-13298529:
Book smarts do not keep tea plants running; cash smarts do. Musa Gün and Mustafa Savcı make that case in a 2026 survey of tea firms in Rize, Türkiye. They asked 203 top staff at 86 tea plants about what they know, what they can do, and how cash flows.

On a ten-point test of book knowledge, staff scored just 4.47 on mean. Yet 85% rated their own skill high. Hands-on skill, such as budgets and cash plans, tied to felt cash strength with a weight of 0.336. Day-to-day cash woes, by contrast, tied to none of the firm traits. The team read that as a sign of season-wide cash strain and urge hands-on training plus steadier loan paths.
pmc-13299429:
Andrés Godoy-Cumillaf and colleagues ask whether longer teaching careers track with body fat and quality of life, in a 2026 cross-sectional study from Temuco, Chile. After accounting for age and sex, those links faded and lost significance, and quality-of-life scores showed no adjusted association either. Teachers overall carried high fat levels and an unfavourable perceived health profile. The authors conclude age, not career length itself, explains the pattern, while noting convenience sampling in one city limits the reach of the findings.
pmc-13299629:
Salazar and colleagues published in twenty twenty-six a study of a muscle protein as a marker in leiomyosarcoma. These cancers grow from smooth muscle and their outlook is hard to predict. In one subgroup, localized grade-two tumors, low levels did link to shorter survival. Mutations appeared in over half the tumors but tied to nothing clear. The authors call the study exploratory. pmc-13299729:

Synergies and antagonisms recur across the evidence. The authors propose designing foods by bioaccessibility rather than ingredient lists, using a Quality by Design framework so that health claims rest on delivery, not just composition.
pmc-13300529:

pmc-13301029:

Progress, the authors argue, needs standard pipelines and proof inside animals more than new strains.
pmc-13302629:

Four hyperbaric oxygen sessions shrank the trapped gas, and her vision normalized eight days after discharge, after a brief myopic shift the authors tie to the oxygen therapy itself. They propose the mediastinal and facial air paralyzed her pupils' near response.
pmc-13303329:

Working in the edge-based framework for SIR spread, they define three running gauges. pmc-13303729:
Yiyan Lin and colleagues design bone-inspired porous structures that must carry load and manage sound at once in a 2026 engineering study. Standard porous materials rarely do both jobs well together.

The Diamond layout gave the best mix of strength, energy uptake, and even performance in all directions. Tube tests also gave Diamond the strongest sound absorption and blocking at high pitches. Tuning the internal layout can thus serve mechanical and acoustic goals together.
pmc-13304129:

The combined changes add up to a green route toward useful alkyl chemicals.
pmc-13304229:

Their weight paths still diverged, tracking gaps and delays in getting and keeping the medicine. Puberty stage, sex, body makeup, and activity also shape results, so single weight numbers need careful reading.
pmc-13305529:
Maria-Teodora Pițuru and co-authors build sponge-like wound dressings from collagen and methylcellulose carrying an anti-inflammatory drug in a 2026 materials study. Biopolymer sponges can deliver medicine right onto wounds while soaking up fluid.

Gels in varied ratios were freeze-dried into porous mats and checked by infrared scans, microscopy, touch angle, and soaking tests. Collagen's natural twist survived in blends up to a quarter methylcellulose, while more of it shrank pores and strengthened the mat. Enzyme breakdown, drug release, and burn tests in rats rounded out the checks for dressing readiness.
pmc-13305629:

pmc-13306629:
Jun Yang and colleagues present a 2026 image fusion framework that helps roadside sensors see targets clearly under harsh lighting. On two public datasets, edge information transfer improved by roughly fifty to over one hundred percent against existing methods. Fused images gave object detection systems more distinctive input features afterwards. The authors built the framework for machine perception rather than human viewing. Stable target outlines in tunnels, night streets, and headlight glare are the practical payoff they claim.
pmc-13306729:
Yonghao Li built a live multi-robot mapping system on 4D Gaussian splatting in a 2026 study. Teams of agents could keep maps fresh over time, yet moving objects and out-of-sync views often corrupt shared updates.

The DGOMapping design couples uncertainty into the scene model and lets agents trade perception scores for each Gaussian point. Conflicting updates get damped rather than amplified, and long-term memory adjusts as scenes change. pmc-13306829:
Alejandro Castellanos and a large Spanish team test in 2026 which wearable choices matter most for reading human activity from motion sensors. Adding gyroscope signals lifted results across setups, and weight checks backed their value. Findings come from lab sessions aligned with a national cohort design. The authors offer the results as design guidance for large studies that plan to track daily motion with wearables.
pmc-13307029:
Yiheng Zhou simulated silicone rubber decay under heat, damp and electric stress together in a 2026 study. The rubber insulates outdoor power gear, where long service brings chalking, cracking and loss of water-repelling behaviour.

A crosslinked molecular model was built and relaxed, then reactive dynamics ran across heat levels, field strengths and ageing plus recovery stages. Tracking carbon and silicon content plus small breakdown products revealed how bonds break under combined stress. The atom-level view explains surface damage patterns seen on bushings and insulators in the field. The small scale tests show the chain works step by step as planned by the team.
pmc-13307429:
Tonny Acire and a very large team pool evidence in 2026 on blocked leg arteries among diabetic foot ulcer patients in poorer countries. pmc-13308529:

Record keeping and faith group outreach could lift cover most.
pmc-13308729:
Chong Huang and co-authors hunt in 2026 cause genes for glioblastoma, a fierce brain tumour, by fusing single cell gene reads with a gene based cause method. They sifted genes that stood out in tumour data, built a risk score, and checked the calls with immune maps and lab assays.

Two genes, CKAP4 and PFDN5, showed direct cause links in the gene based tests and lit up in tumour cells alone. Both may serve as fresh marks and drug targets, and the joint method may speed like hunts in other cancers.
pmc-13309029:
Muhammad Saiful Islam Khan and co-authors test a claim in 2026, that water treated by a microplasma device can strip farm spray residue from perilla leaves and broccoli. Plasma water and chlorine water each cleared 80.84 to 87.17 percent of spray from leaves, and 51.74 to 67.77 percent from broccoli in the lab checks. Cold water at 10 degrees boosted plasma wash gains, while chlorine wash lost ground in the cold. No wash changed the colour of the goods, even after a week in a fridge.
pmc-13310529:

The authors warn that zirconia neighbours deserve extra diagnostic caution when resorption is suspected nearby.
pmc-13310929:
